"It would be great," they told me. "Three square meals, a roof over my head, and trips to exotic locales." Instead I got shipped off to the middle of nowhere. Not that I have an objection to nowhere, just that there isn't much to do here except survive. Maybe thrive too. I haven't decided on that bit yet.

But anyways, my company was sent to the middle of nowhere. An entire company sent to nowhere -- absolute madness I tell you! It was supposed to be a basic mission: scout and patrol the area; make sure nobody comes inside. A great plan in theory, but who would come? We're in the middle of nowhere. It's a begging swamp! There's not enough dry socks in the world to make a sane person want to come here.

Anyways, the company is on the mission to simply scout and patrol, and we are given supplies. A ton of supplies. Guns, ammo, water, food. Even some extra clothing and blankets. Heck, there's a ton more than that, and I could never figure out why they sent us here with so much stuff. An entire company, to nowhere, with five shipping crates of stuff dropped into the swamps. One of them even had precious art. No clue why, but it did.

Four days into the mission, the ground rumbles. A slow but distant roar at first, but soon the terra is dancing like she wanted to do a jig. Trees topple, the waters ripple, and the laughable fort we are staying at goes from looking bad to looking worse. Company commander calls in to HQ on the radio to see what the hell is going on. HQ just tells us to continue with our mission. That it was nothing more than an asteroid strike. Or three. Maybe seven. Regardless, it was nothing for us to worry about, and we should continue with our mission. Logistics would be dropping off more supplies later in the week.

It only took a day for the sky to turn dark. Hazy even. Nobody knows where the asteroid hit, but the swamp smelled of dust and burning. There's an irony in there somewhere. Still, we do our patrols until Logistics comes in with more supplies, and sure enough, they do. Ninety-six giant containers of supplies. A good number of them are food and rations, but some of the containers are welded shut and padlocked. Told not to open them.

Communication with HQ after the drop-off just kinda died. Never heard a word from them again. Only took a month for people to speculate what had happened. Took just as long for us to speculate that we're not here on a patrol mission, but to protect whatever is inside the locked containers. Took us less than a month after that before the Captain himself blasted a hole in one of the sealed crates only to find it filled with books. Classical literature, science journals, a whole gamut of information. A copy of "Where the Red Fern Grows" sadly didn't survive the blast.

Routine is what saved me. Just stick to the same thing. Don't think about the lack of outside communication. Lots of men in the company did, and they tried to mutiny. Mutiny is punishable by death. It was punished by death. Every month the company grew smaller. People just went insane. Dreamed up conspiracies. Can't say I blame them, as even I figured out what was going on. We're here to protect knowledge of the world. Art, literature, science, philosophy. All things that likely wouldn't survive an asteroid impact. Or three. Or seven.

Now, it is just me. Every morning I follow my routine, and slowly the fog of war lifts. Every evening I can see a bit further into the horizon. Maybe soon Logistics will return to take the crates back. Until then, I'll just follow my routine. Just survive. Probably not thrive.

I've been enjoying xcom enemy within on android lately.

Distant Worlds: Universe

It's not particularly price friendly, but I think its novelty makes it worth it. It essentially takes the strategic complexity of a turn based strategy and combines it with the dynamic real time interactions of an RTS all on a ridiculously huge scale. A single game might take days if not weeks. It's impossible for a single human to manage your entire empire so there are automation options available essentially everything. It's actually possible to let the AI take over everything. The idea being that you can do better. The learning curve is brutal but the game is incredibly rewarding once you get over that initial hump.

If you have an iPad I must recommend Imperium Galactica 2 (it's a great hybrid that is somewhat akin to Star Wars: Empire at War, but with a deeper 4x angle) and Starbase Orion (basically Master of Orion 2). Another great hybrid, as mentioned by Ulluses is Sins of a Solar Empire. I've sunk plenty of hours into the game and it's a great fleet battle game.

For a pure 4x experience your best options are Galactic Civilizations 2 (3 will hopefully be out of early-alpha sometime soon), and Endless Space (so long as you get the expansion). At this point I tend towards playing Endless Space as I'm a big fan of their lore after playing both is and Endless Legend. There are also other older games to play, like Master of Orion 2/3, but they've become a lot more difficult to play over time as players get comfortable with modern UIs.
